note.subject: biology
note.title: Bacteria and division
note.overview: Describe bacterial structure and growth by binary fission; use the doubling model correctly.
learningGoals: Explain the key idea using school examples.
Apply it to a short-answer or calculation question.
mustMemoriseRules: Bacteria are prokaryotes with no membrane-bound nucleus. Some have plasmids.
In binary fission the DNA is copied, the cell grows and two daughter cells form.
Under ideal conditions, population = starting population × 2^(number of rounds). Real growth is limited by conditions.
detailedExplanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes with no membrane-bound nucleus. Some have plasmids.
In binary fission the DNA is copied, the cell grows and two daughter cells form.
Under ideal conditions, population = starting population × 2^(number of rounds). Real growth is limited by conditions.

workedExamples.answer: One cell to 128 cells takes seven rounds because 2⁷ = 128. At 30 minutes per round this is 3.5 hours.
workedExamples.why: Follow the units and the biological reason given in the explanation.

commonMistakes: Do not count 128 divisions for a final population of 128.
Do not describe bacterial division as mitosis of a nucleus.
